Reference Number: POC-6B4F896296-38363
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-19
Service at Issue: Cervical fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
Appeal Deadline: Must be received by 2027-02-15

To the Moda Health Appeal Unit:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (CPT 22551), as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-19. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity." I am requesting that Moda Health reverse this determination and approve the surgery.

Moda Health's own provider-facing materials state that authorizations for musculoskeletal and spine surgery services, which includes CPT 22551, are obtained through EviCore, a Moda Health partner, and that the applicable clinical guidelines are published by EviCore. The EviCore guideline document addressing this exact procedure is "CMM-601: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion Guidelines" (Version 2.0.2024, effective November 1, 2024). I am relying on the language of that document below because it is the only medical-necessity criteria document I have been able to locate that specifically governs CPT 22551 under this plan's authorization program. If a different or more specific policy or criteria set was actually applied to my case, I am formally requesting that Moda Health provide me with the complete text of that document, including its title, policy number, and effective date, so that I may respond to it directly.

Based on the CMM-601 guideline, "Initial primary anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) is considered medically necessary when performed for EITHER of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met," including a "Radiculopathy" pathway. My clinical record satisfies each element of that pathway as follows:

1. Subjective symptoms. The guideline requires "BOTH of the following: Significant level of pain on a daily basis defined as clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing, etc.)" and "Unremitting radicular pain to shoulder girdle and/or upper extremity resulting in disability." My records document 24 months of progressive neck pain unrelieved by rest, together with radicular pain and numbness radiating into my right thumb and index finger accompanied by weakness — symptoms that have interfered with my daily functioning.

2. Objective physical exam findings. The guideline requires "ANY of the following: Dermatomal sensory deficit; Motor deficit (e.g., biceps, triceps weakness); Reflex changes; Shoulder abduction relief sign; Nerve root tension sign (e.g., Spurling's maneuver)." My exam findings include a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level and positive provocative testing on the affected side, along with the weakness noted above.

3. Conservative treatment trial. The guideline requires "Less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated): Prescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or NSAIDs for 6 weeks; Provider-directed exercise program (prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider, osteopathic or allopathic physician) for 6 weeks; Epidural steroid injection(s) or selective nerve root block(s) performed at the same level(s) as the requested surgery." I completed NSAID therapy for 8 months with inadequate relief; a supervised physical therapy program including cervical traction and postural training for 10 weeks (2026-04-30 through 2026-07-09, 20 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note); and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-14 that provided only 3 weeks of partial relief. This satisfies, and exceeds, the requirement of at least two qualifying conservative measures without clinically meaningful improvement.

4. Imaging. The guideline requires that "MRI/CT shows neural structure compression at the requested level(s) that is concordant with the individual's symptoms and physical exam findings and that is caused by ANY of the following: Herniated disc(s) (retained disc material or a recurrent disc herniation); Synovial cyst or arachnoid cyst; Central/lateral/foraminal stenosis; Osteophytes." My MRI of the cervical spine dated 2026-06-05 shows a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression, which is concordant with my right thumb/index finger radicular pattern and my weakness on examination.

5. Absence of unmanaged behavioral health/substance use disorder. The guideline requires "Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders)." My record documents no active infection and no untreated substance use.

6. Nicotine status. The guideline requires "Documentation of nicotine-free status with EITHER of the following: Individual is a never-smoker; [or cessation for at least 6 weeks with confirmatory lab values]." I am a non-smoker.

Taken together, my clinical record — 24 months of progressive symptoms, a completed and well-documented conservative treatment trial (8 months of NSAIDs, 10 weeks/20 visits of supervised physical therapy, and a corticosteroid injection with only transient partial relief), concordant imaging showing C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression, a corresponding neurologic deficit, positive provocative testing, and the absence of any disqualifying comorbidity — meets each element of the Radiculopathy pathway of the ACDF criteria quoted above.

I am enclosing the following supporting documentation with this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-30 to 2026-07-09)
- Medication history documenting NSAID trial
- Procedure note for corticosteroid injection dated 2026-05-14
- MRI cervical spine report dated 2026-06-05
- Office visit notes documenting exam findings, provocative testing, and neurologic deficit
- Letter of medical necessity from [Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery / surgeon's practice name and contact information]

I respectfully request that Moda Health reverse the denial of CPT 22551 and approve the requested anterior cervical discectomy and fusion. I further request, pursuant to my appeal rights, a copy of the complete, specific medical policy or clinical criteria document actually relied upon in the original denial, including its title, policy/document number, and effective date, if it differs from the EviCore CMM-601 guideline cited above.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the anticipated timeframe for a decision. If you have any questions or require additional information, please contact me at [phone number] or [email address], or my surgeon's office at [surgeon office phone/fax].

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Avery Grant
